decisions.reason: Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN (workbook Methods!D133) reads DS.VISITNUM only where DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED', and adsl-probe.yaml P4_COMPLETE keeps that spelling verbatim. The staged DS spells the completion term PROTOCOL COMPLETED, so the literal probe is missing on every record where the reference holds a visit number.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT takes SV.SVSTDTC where SV.VISITNUM=3, while TRTSDT imputes EX_MINDTC, MIN(EX.EXSTDTC) at adsl_v1.yaml lines 317-322. The source domain and the visit condition differ, not only their wording.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT substitutes the discontinuation date only when the final dose date is missing and the subject discontinued after visit 3. The TRTEDT case at adsl_v1.yaml lines 344-348 takes DS_DISP.DSSTDTC whenever LAST_EXENDTC is missing, with no discontinuation or visit condition.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE computes the dose per arm from TRT01PN and visit-delimited dosing intervals. CUMDOSE at adsl_v1.yaml lines 371-443 instead sums EXDOSE times record days over EX and extends an open last record to TRTEDT, a different computation.

Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1 (workbook Methods!D89) names ADSL.AGEGR1N as the source of the character group. AGEGR1 at adsl_v1.yaml lines 460-469 reads DM.AGE and never AGEGR1N, which the specification instead derives from AGEGR1.

Through the AGEGR1 element (adsl_v1.yaml lines 460-469), the AGEGR1N mapping applies the AGE thresholds <65, 65-80 and >80 and the codes 1, 2 and 3 of Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1N, so this method's source and computation have a counterpart. The reversed AGEGR1/AGEGR1N direction is the subject of ADSL.AGEGR1.CR-6.1, not a difference in this method.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP8FL compares ENDDT with the visit 8 date, and ENDDT is defined in no define section, workbook sheet or ADRG page. COMP8FL at adsl_v1.yaml line 583 compares RFENDT, so the end date is the specification's choice rather than a stated counterpart.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP16FL compares ENDDT with the visit 10 date, and ENDDT is defined in no define section, workbook sheet or ADRG page. COMP16FL at adsl_v1.yaml line 608 compares RFENDT, so the end date is the specification's choice rather than a stated counterpart.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL compares ENDDT with the visit 12 date, and ENDDT is defined in no define section, workbook sheet or ADRG page. COMP24FL at adsl_v1.yaml line 633 compares RFENDT, so the end date is the specification's choice rather than a stated counterpart.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS (workbook Methods!D106) measures from DISONSET, which is not an ADSL variable and appears nowhere else in the retained documents. DURDIS_DAYS at adsl_v1.yaml line 772 starts at DISONSDT, a repair of the documented source that no document states.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDSGR1 groups DURDIS values as <12 and >=12, which places a missing duration in neither group. The otherwise branch at adsl_v1.yaml line 789 also assigns >=12 when DURDIS is missing.

Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN reads DS.VISITNUM only where DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED'. VISNUMEN at adsl_v1.yaml lines 796-803 remaps the visit of the first DSCAT='DISPOSITION EVENT' record (DS_DISP, lines 185-194) with no DSTERM condition.
Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT sums QS.QSORRES, the original result. MMSETOT at adsl_v1.yaml line 810 sums QS.QSSTRESN, the standardized result, a different source variable.

The retained define-adam.xml ItemDef IT.ADSL.STUDYID carries a Predecessor origin DM.STUDYID (line 596), and workbook Variables!M143/P143 repeat it; the exported ADSL.STUDYID section omits origins. The derivation DM.STUDYID is therefore stated in a retained document.

The retained define-adam.xml ItemDef IT.ADSL.USUBJID carries a Predecessor origin DM.USUBJID (line 607), and workbook Variables!M144/P144 repeat it; the exported ADSL.USUBJID section omits origins. The derivation DM.USUBJID is therefore stated in a retained document.

Define-XML ADSL.SITEGR1 (workbook Methods!D122) states only the pooled and unpooled values and refers to SAP Section 7.1. No retained section or workbook sheet lists the pooled site set, and the shared SAP is pending_review in submission-pilot5/spec/source/manifest.json.

Define-XML ADSL.SITEGR1 says SITEGR1 is 900 if pooled but leaves which sites are pooled to SAP Section 7.1. That SAP is listed with pending_review applicability in submission-pilot5/spec/source/manifest.json, so no retained document supplies the pooling condition.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT only converts the visit date to a SAS date and states no completion of partial dates. The only imputation rule in the retained documents, ADRG page-5 section 3.4, concerns ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE (workbook Methods!D99) branches on ARMN=0, 1 and 2 although CL.ARMN codes the arms 0, 54 and 81, and it uses TRTSTDT, visit4date and visit12date, which no retained document defines. A literal probe would have to choose the arm mapping, the start date and the visit-date sources.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP8FL (workbook Methods!D98) compares ENDDT with the visit 8 date, and ENDDT is not an ADSL variable and is defined in no define section, workbook sheet or ADRG page. The comparison cannot be stated literally without choosing which date ENDDT is.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP16FL (workbook Methods!D96) compares ENDDT with the visit 10 date, and ENDDT is not an ADSL variable and is defined in no define section, workbook sheet or ADRG page. The comparison cannot be stated literally without choosing which date ENDDT is.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL (workbook Methods!D97) compares ENDDT with the visit 12 date, and ENDDT is not an ADSL variable and is defined in no define section, workbook sheet or ADRG page. The comparison cannot be stated literally without choosing which date ENDDT is.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL (workbook Methods!D94) gives WEIGHTBL / ((HEIGHTBL/100)**2) with no zero-height condition. No retained section states the NULLIF(HEIGHTBL, 0) guard of BMIBL_RAW at adsl_v1.yaml line 709.

Define-XML ADSL.WEIGHTBL (workbook Methods!D134) names the test and visit but no rule for several qualifying records. No retained section states the lowest-VISITNUM, keep-first selection of BASE_WT at adsl_v1.yaml lines 126-129.

Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL (workbook Methods!D108) identifies SCTESTCD=EDLEVEL without choosing among several records. No retained section states the SCSEQ keep-first selection of SC_EDU at adsl_v1.yaml lines 202-205.

Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT (workbook Methods!D103) converts MH.MHSTDTC to a SAS date without completing partial dates. No retained section states the month 1, day 1 completion at adsl_v1.yaml lines 746-747; ADRG page-5 section 3.4 covers only ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT (workbook Methods!D103) selects MHCAT='PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS' without choosing among several such records. No retained section states the MHSEQ keep-first selection of MH_DX at adsl_v1.yaml lines 213-216.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS (workbook Methods!D106) asks for the number of months between two dates and says nothing of counting days inclusively. No retained section states the closed-both day difference of DURDIS_DAYS at adsl_v1.yaml lines 774-775.
Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS (workbook Methods!D106) does not define the length of a month. No retained section states the 30.4375-day month of DURDIS at adsl_v1.yaml line 780.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS (workbook Methods!D106) measures from DISONSET, which is not an ADSL variable, and does not say whether months are calendar, average or fractional. A literal probe would have to repair the source name and choose a month convention.

Define-XML ADSL.VISIT1DT (workbook Methods!D132) converts SV.SVSTDTC to a SAS date without completing partial dates. No retained section states the month 1, day 1 completion at adsl_v1.yaml lines 762-763.

Define-XML ADSL.VISIT1DT (workbook Methods!D132) names the visit 1 record but no rule for several such records. SV1 at adsl_v1.yaml lines 147-150 orders by VISITNUM and keeps the first, a selection no retained section states.

Define-XML ADSL.DCDECOD (workbook Methods!D100) selects DSCAT='DISPOSITION EVENT' without choosing among several such records. No retained section states the DSSEQ keep-first selection of DS_DISP at adsl_v1.yaml lines 191-194.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS says to group DCDECOD values, and CL.DISCREAS decodes I/E Not Met only to itself, with no source condition. No retained section or workbook sheet states the DSTERM='PROTOCOL ENTRY CRITERIA NOT MET' override of DCREASCD at adsl_v1.yaml lines 669-670.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS and CL.DISCREAS list Completed as a coded value and say nothing of leaving the reason blank. No retained section or workbook sheet states the empty reason for completed subjects at adsl_v2.yaml lines 672-673.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS (workbook Methods!D101) says only to group DCDECOD values; CL.DISCREAS decodes most groups to DCDECOD terms, but I/E Not Met decodes to itself and no retained section names the records it groups. A literal probe would have to supply that condition and the completed-subject value.

Define-XML ADSL.DISCONFL (workbook Methods!D102) compares DCREASCD with Completed, and the original ItemRef IT.ADSL.DCSREAS (define-adam.xml lines 275-276) and Variables!O190 bind the DCREASCD method to DCSREAS, so the probe's REF.DCSREAS reading is the rule as written. The reference leaves DCSREAS blank for the 110 reported subjects, so the documented inequality flags them Y where the reference flag is empty.

Define-XML ADSL.DISCONFL's 'Null otherwise' denotes an unpopulated flag, and the published reference stores every unflagged DISCONFL as empty text, which ADRG page-36 lists beside null as a Dataset-JSON v1.1 missing-value representation. The otherwise branch at adsl_v1.yaml line 680 reproduces that representation rather than stating a different rule.

Define-XML ADSL.RACEN and its CL.RACEN codelist (workbook Codelists rows 258-262) code ASIAN as 7 and NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER as 5. The RACEN mapping at adsl_v1.yaml lines 496-501 lists only the other three races, so those two codes have no counterpart even though the staged data hold neither race.

Define-XML ADSL.HEIGHTBL requires VS.VISITNUM=1. BASE_HT at adsl_v1.yaml lines 109-118 filters only VSTESTCD='HEIGHT' and keeps the lowest VISITNUM, so it would take a height first recorded at another visit.

Define-XML ADSL.WEIGHTBL selects the VS.VISITNUM=3 record. BASE_WT at adsl_v1.yaml line 125 selects VSBLFL='Y' instead, a different record condition even where the flagged record is the visit 3 record.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT says to convert the final dose date to a SAS date without completing partial dates. No retained section states the month 1, day 1 completion of LAST_EXENDTC at adsl_v1.yaml lines 355-357; ADRG page-5 section 3.4 covers only ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.RFENDT (workbook Methods!D117) converts RFENDTC to a SAS date without completing partial dates. No retained section states the month 1, day 1 completion at adsl_v1.yaml lines 574-575; ADRG page-5 section 3.4 covers only ADAE.ASTDT.

missed.quote: All patients in DM were included in ADSL.
missed.reason: No claim cites this dataset-population statement; the treated-subjects row rule filters DM.ACTARM to exclude Screen Failure. Original Define-XML IG.ADSL def:Structure at line 182 and workbook Datasets!D5 instead explicitly exclude Screen Failures, so this statement also needs document-to-document reconciliation.

missed.quote: Are the values of ARM equivalent in meaning to values of TRT01P? Yes.
missed.reason: No claim cites this statement that TRT01P carries the values of ARM; it agrees with Define-XML ADSL.TRT01P (DM.ARM) and the specification's TRT01P derivation from DM.ARM.
